svg.aria-label: Block diagram of one Three Columns page. A dashed band at the top, labeled SITE-UNIQUE, holds the masthead: the 3Col mark and eyebrow, the title, the What this is label and standfirst, the attributes line, and the picture slot with its 22 pixel caption. Below it a strip of standard controls: the A, B and C tabs, search, Phone view, Save as PDF and Dark. Then the threshold, a double rule with the 3Col mark knocking a gap in it, captioned Everything below is the same on every 3Col site. Below the threshold, labeled 3COL STANDARD, are three switches that turn each column on or off, then the three columns themselves: A Plain answers in green, a stack of questions that open, widening downward from plain to more detailed; B Sources in gold, holding Internal links and External links with the six-part source card, in a constant register that does not widen; and C How it works in red, widening downward from assumed know-how to more technical. Red numerals in A and C point across to source cards in B, and a Back control returns. A bottom strip gives the three renderings, the meaning of the three colors, and the size of the whole thing.

g.text: The title of this one site
One paragraph that says what the site is for,
and one example you can go and look at.
free to host · nothing to hack · works on any device · you own it
The picture, and its caption at 22 px
— often the only line a scanner reads

svg.text: Everything inside this band changes from site to site. Nothing else does.
the controls are standard too — each one its own small script

g.text: Everything below is the same on every 3Col site
the reader turns any column off · the markup is the setting, so no script is involved
each one closed until it is opened.
+ How do I change the words later?
Two blocks, always in this order,
worded the same on every site.
The two most recent content changes.
Every reference to some other website.
4 preview — what you would find there
5 why it is cited — in THIS page
6 the link, last and only last
one register throughout — it does not deepen
a numeral in A or C lands on its card · Back returns you to it
Prior know-how is assumed, and more
of it is assumed as you go down.
The shape — one file, four scripts
Why the sources sit in the middle
The anatomy of a source card
wide · narrow · printed — one markup, nothing duplicated
gold — the column keys, and where you are
red — citations, and whatever a click just reached
a dead link turns gray and is struck through
no framework, no build step, no database
drop one and only its control goes
